# Didache Chapter 4 — The EMET Bible (Literal)

**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Codex Hierosolymitanus (H), Didache 4 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/DID_004_page_001.jpg

---

## Chapter 4

**1** My child, remember night and day the one who speaks to you the word of God, and honor him as the Lord — for wherever the lordly nature is spoken of, there the Lord is.

**2** And you shall seek out daily the faces of the saints, so that you may rest upon their words.

**3** You shall not cause a division, but you shall make peace between those who quarrel. You shall judge righteously; you shall not show partiality when reproving transgressions.

**4** You shall not be double-minded about whether something will be or not.

**5** Do not be one who stretches out his hands to receive but draws them back when it comes to giving.

**6** If you have the means of your hands, you shall give a ransom for your sins.

**7** You shall not hesitate to give, nor shall you grumble when giving — for you will know who is the good paymaster of the reward.

**8** You shall not turn away from one who is in need, but you shall share all things with your brother, and you shall not say that they are your own; for if you are partners in what is immortal, how much more in mortal things?

**9** You shall not remove your hand from your son or from your daughter, but from their youth you shall teach them the fear of God.

**10** You shall not command in bitterness your male slave or your female slave who hope in the same God as you, lest they cease to fear the God who is over you both; for he comes not to call according to reputation, but upon those whom the Spirit has prepared.

**11** But you, slaves — be subject to your masters as to God, in shame and fear.

**12** You shall hate all hypocrisy and everything that is not pleasing to the Lord.

**13** You shall not forsake the commandments of the Lord, but you shall keep the things you received, neither adding to them nor taking away from them.

**14** In the assembly you shall confess your transgressions, and you shall not come forward to your prayer with an evil conscience. This is the way of life.

---

*EMET notes: V.1 — "lordly nature" = τὸ κυριακὸν τῆς κυριότητος, a dense phrase linking the teacher's message with the Lord's own authority. V.6 — "ransom for your sins" = λύτρον τῶν ἁμαρτιῶν σου; almsgiving as atonement, a Jewish concept (cf. Sir 3:30; Tob 12:9). V.10 — "comes not to call according to reputation" = God shows no favoritism (prosōpolēmpsia). V.14 — "assembly" = ἐκκλησία.*
